Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כל היכא דתני הכל, כולהו מייתי להו בשמעתא קמייתא דערכין, ומפרש הכל לאתויי מאי. והכל שוחטין דמתניתין פליגי בה אמוראי בגמרא, למר לאתויי טמא בחולין, ולמר לאתויי כותי או מומר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - Wherever [the Mishnah] teaches "all," they all bring [the discussion of] them in the first sugya of tractate Arachin, and it explains: "all" comes to include what? And [as for] "all may slaughter" in our Mishnah, the amoraim disagree about it in the Gemara: according to one, it comes to include a ritually impure person [slaughtering] non-sacred animals, and according to the other, it comes to include a Samaritan (Kuthite) or an apostate.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: And all of them - The Gemara explains what "all of them" [means].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.hebrew: ושחיטתן כשרה דיעבד - בתמיה. וקשה: רישא דמשמע דההוא דאתרבי מהכל לכתחלה אתרבי, ואילו סיפא משמע דכי מרבינן מהכל דיעבד מרבינן לה, אבל לכתחלה לא אתרבי. והא ליכא למימר כולה מתניתין לכתחלה וחדא קתני, דכיון דתנא הכל שוחטין פשיטא דכשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.english: And their slaughter is valid after the fact - [This is said] as a question. And this is difficult: the beginning [of the Mishnah] implies that the one who is included by [the word] "all" is included ab initio (le-chatchilah), whereas the end implies that when we include [someone] by [the word] "all," we include him [only] after the fact (bediavad), but ab initio he is not included. And one cannot say that the entire Mishnah speaks of [the case] ab initio and is teaching a single [consistent] rule, since once it taught "all may slaughter," it is obvious that [the slaughter] is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.hebrew: וכל הכל לכתחלה הוא - דתקשה לך ולא תוכל לומר כולה דיעבד, וה"ק, הכל תורת שחיטה נוהגת בהן, שאם שחטו אותן הפסולין דמתרבי תהא שחיטתן כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.english: And [the reason the Mishnah says] "all" is [to teach the law applies] ab initio - for [otherwise] it would be difficult for you, and you could not say that all of it [refers only to the case] after the fact; rather, this is what [the Mishnah] means: the law of [proper] slaughter applies to them, so that if these disqualified [individuals] who are included [by the word "all"] slaughtered [an animal], their slaughter is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.hebrew: אלא הכל ממירים - מי מצית למימר לכתחלה יביא בהמת חולין אצל בהמת קדשים ויאמר זו תמורת זו? הכל דתמורה מפרש התם לאתויי יורש שממיר בקרבן אביו לאחר מיתת אביו, דהתם תנן: אין ממירין בשל אחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.english: Rather, all substitute - Could you possibly say that, ab initio, one may bring a non-sacred animal next to a consecrated animal and say, "This one is a substitute for that one"? [No, since that is forbidden.] Rather, "all," regarding substitution, is explained there [in tractate Temurah] to include an heir who substitutes [an animal] for his father's offering after his father's death, since we learned there: one may not effect a substitution with another's [offering].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:3.english: Good - [i.e.,] innocent [one who has not made a vow at all is considered blameless].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - דעקר להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא, אבל הכל שוחטין בדוכתיה קאי, דכל כמה דלא עקר ליה ותנא לא שיהו הפסולים רשאים לשחוט כדעקר התם, משמע דלכתחלה רבינהו, והדר תני ושחיטתן כשרה, דמשמע דיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, since it teaches the reason - [The stated reason] uproots [the implication of] the "all" of the first clause [of the Mishnah in Temurah], so that you should not say it is permitted ab initio. But [in our Mishnah,] "all may slaughter" stands in its place, for as long as [the Mishnah] has not uprooted it and taught, "not that the disqualified are permitted to slaughter," as it uprooted [that implication] there, it implies that it included them [the disqualified] ab initio. And then it teaches, "and their slaughter is valid," which implies after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: לא שהאדם רשאי - דכתיב "לא יחליפנו", ורישא הכי קאמר: הכל דין תמורה נוהגת בהם. והא דתנא ברישא "הכל ממירין", ואיצטריך ליה תו לפרושי "לא שהאדם רשאי" כו', ולא נקט ברישא לשון קצרה "הכל שהמירו תמורתם תמורה" - לשון התנאים הוא זה, כמו "הכל שוחטין", "הכל סומכין", "הכל חייבין", הלכך הכא אע"ג דהוצרך להאריך לא שינה התנא את לשונו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: Not that a person is permitted - since it is written, "he shall not exchange it," and the opening clause means this: the law of substitution (temurah) applies to them [i.e., if one does substitute, the substitution takes effect]. And as for the fact that it taught at the outset, "All may effect a substitution," and then needed to further explain, "not that a person is permitted," etc. - and did not use at the outset the terse formulation, "Whoever effected a substitution, their substitution takes effect" - this is the style of the Tannaim, like "All may slaughter," "All may perform semikhah," "All are obligated." Therefore here, even though it had to elaborate, the Tanna did not depart from his style.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:3.english: The substitution takes effect [mumar] - The second [animal, the non-sacred one substituted] becomes caught [in sanctity], and both of them are holy.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:4.english: And he incurs the forty [lashes] - On account of the prohibition, "he shall not substitute."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.hebrew: הכל מעריכין - התם מפרש לאתויי מופלא סמוך לאיש, קטן היודע להפלות לשם מי מקדישין, ואם סמוך לפרקו הוא, כגון בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד, דבריו קיימין, אע"פ שעדיין קטן הוא עד י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.english: All may vow valuations - There [in the first Mishnah of Arachin], it explains that [the word] "all" comes to include a mufla samuch le'ish - a minor who knows how to discern for whom he is consecrating. And if he is close to his maturity, such as one who is twelve years and one day old, his words are valid, even though he is still legally a minor until thirteen years and one day.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.hebrew: מעריכין - תורת מעריכין עליהם, שאם אמר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי נדרו קיים, ואע"ג דקטן הוא זה הנודר, חייב ליתן כפי שנים של נערך, והדמים קצובין בפרשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.english: Vow valuations - The law of vowing valuations applies to them, that if one said, "My valuation is upon me," or "So-and-so's valuation is upon me," his vow is valid. And even though the one making the vow is a minor, he is obligated to give according to the years of the one being valuated, and the sums are fixed in the Torah portion.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.hebrew: הכל נערכין - יש להם ערך, ואפילו מוכה שחין שאינו שוה כלום לימכר בשוק, יש לו ערך הכתוב בפרשה. ואם אמר על עצמו ערכי עלי, או אמר על אחר ערך מוכה שחין זה עלי, לא אמרינן הואיל ודמים אין לו, ערך נמי אין לו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.english: All are subject to valuation - They have a [fixed Torah] value; and even one afflicted with boils, who is worth nothing to be sold in the marketplace, has the value written in the [Torah] portion. And if one said about himself, "my valuation is upon me," or said about another, "the valuation of this boil-afflicted person is upon me," we do not say: since he has no monetary worth, he also has no [fixed Torah] value.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.hebrew: הכל נודרים - דמי עלי או דמי פלוני עלי. והתם מפרש, דאיידי דבעי למיתני הכל נידרין, תנא נמי הכל נודרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.english: All vow - [meaning one says,] "My value is incumbent upon me," or "So-and-so's value is incumbent upon me." And there [in tractate Arachin], it is explained that since [the Mishnah] needed to teach "all are the object of such a vow," it also taught "all vow."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.hebrew: הכל נידרים - כל אדם השוה כלום, יש לו דמים, ואם אמר דמי עלי, או אמר על אחר דמי פלוני עלי, נותן לפי מה שהוא נמכר בשוק. ואפילו היה הנידר זה פחות מבן חדש, ואמר דמי תינוק זה עלי, יתן דמיו, ואע"פ שאין פחות מבן חדש נערך. ואם אמר ערכו עלי, פטור מכלום, שלא נתנה בו תורה ערך, דכתיב (ויקרא כז) ואם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים - דמים מיהא יש לו לפי שויו, ואם אמר בתורת דמים, נותן דמיו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.english: All may be [the subject of] a value-vow - Any person who has some worth has a "damim" [market value]. And if one said, "His damim is upon me," or said of another, "So-and-so's damim is upon me," he pays according to what he would sell for in the market. And even if the one vowed upon was less than a month old, and he said, "This infant's damim is upon me," he must pay his damim, even though a child less than a month old is not subject to an erech [fixed Torah valuation]. But if he said, "His erech is upon me," he is exempt from anything, for the Torah did not assign an erech to him, since it is written (Leviticus 27) "and if from a month old to five years old" [the Torah's erech table begins only at one month] - nevertheless, he does have a damim [market value] according to his worth, and if one said, "in terms of damim," he pays his damim.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:6.english: There will not be sin in you - This implies that if you do make a vow, there will be sin in you [if you fail to pay it].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: טוב אשר לא תדור - לעיל מיניה כתיב את אשר תדור שלם, ואפילו הכי טוב אשר לא תדור, שמא תדור ולא תשלם. הכי מפרש ליה רבי מאיר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: Better that you not vow - Just before this it is written, "That which you vow, fulfill" (Ecclesiastes 5:3), and even so, "better that you not vow" [means] lest you vow and not pay. This is how Rabbi Meir explains it.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה - מנודר ומשלם, ומנודר ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than this and than that - [Meaning: better] than one who vows and pays, and than one who vows and does not pay.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:3.english: That one does not vow at all - For one who is accustomed to making vows comes to [transgress the prohibition of] "he shall not break his word."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר טוב מזה ומזה נודר ומשלם - דהכי משמע: טוב אשר לא תדור משתדור ולא תשלם, אבל משתדור ותשלם - לא, שהוא טוב מכולם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Better than both is one who vows and pays - For this is what [the verse] implies: "It is better that you not vow" than [that] you vow and do not pay, but [that it is] better than [one who] vows and pays - no; [it does not mean] that it [not vowing] is better than all of them.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.hebrew: ואפילו ר' יהודה לא קאמר אלא דאמר הרי זו - דאם מתה או נגנבה, אינו חייב באחריותה. אי נמי, כיון דאפרשה, תו לא הדר ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.english: And even Rabbi Yehuda says this only when he states: This is [designated] - For if it dies or is stolen, he is not liable for its loss. Alternatively, since he has already set it aside, he can no longer retract from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כתוב בהלכות ארץ ישראל דנשים לא ישחטו, מפני שדעתן קלות. ואין נראה, דאפילו במוקדשין שוחטות לכתחלה, כדאמרינן פרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) כל הפסולים ששחטו, דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא. ורמינהי: "ושחט", מלמד שהשחיטה כשרה כו', ומשני: הוא הדין דאפילו לכתחלה, אלא משום דבעי למיתני טמא במוקדשים דלכתחלה לא, תנא נמי ששחטו. ולא קאמר משום דבעי למיתני נשים דתנא להו ברישא, אלא ודאי משום דנשים שוחטות לכתחלה אפילו במוקדשין. והא דלא קתני הכל שוחטין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים כדקתני בתמורה (דף ב.), התם אצטריך למיתנייה, כדפירש בריש תמורה, משום דכל הפרשה כולה נאמרה בלשון זכר, אבל הכא אין חידוש באשה יותר מבאיש. ובפרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) גבי קדשים איצטריך למיתני נשים, משום דבשאר עבודות נשים פסולות אפילו כהנות:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: Everyone may slaughter - It is written in Hilchot Eretz Yisrael that women should not slaughter, because their mind is flighty. But this does not seem right, for even with regard to consecrated animals (kodashim) they may slaughter ab initio (lechatchila), as we say in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b): all those who are disqualified who [nevertheless] slaughtered - after the fact (bediavad) it is valid, but not ab initio. And they raise a contradiction: "and he shall slaughter" teaches that the slaughter is valid, etc., and they answer: the same is true even ab initio, but rather, since it needed to teach [the case of] a ritually impure person with regard to consecrated animals, where ab initio is not [permitted], it therefore also phrased it as "who slaughtered" [implying only after the fact]. And [we know] it did not say this because it needed to teach about women - since it had already taught that in the first clause (reisha) - but rather it is certainly because women may slaughter ab initio even with regard to consecrated animals. And as for why it does not state "everyone may slaughter, both men and women," as it states in Temurah (2a) - there it was necessary to state it, as explained at the beginning of Temurah, because that entire passage is phrased in the masculine, but here there is no novelty in [including] a woman beyond [including] a man. And in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b), with regard to kodashim, it was necessary to teach [explicitly about] women, because with regard to other rites (avodot), women are disqualified, even [if they are] daughters of kohanim (kohanot).

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.hebrew: שמא יקלקלו כו' - בגמרא (לקמן חולין יב:) דייק מדקתני שמא יקלקלו ולא קתני שמא קלקלו, ש"מ אין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה. ופ"ה אפילו אחרים רואין אותן, וק' לפירושו, דהא מסיפא שמעינן לה: וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן כו', דמשמע דיעבד דוקא. וליכא למימר דדיעבד נקט משום טמא במוקדשין או אין מומחין, אבל חש"ו אפילו לכתחלה שוחטין באחרים רואין אותן, דהא רבא הוא דדייק שמא קלקלו לא קתני, ולרבא לא קאי וכולן ששחטו אלא אחש"ו, כדאמרינן בגמרא. וי"מ דגרס לקמן רבה, אבל רבא לא דייק בין יקלקלו לקלקלו, כי היכי דלא חייש בהא דלא קתני ואם שחטו. ור"ת מפרש דאין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה לשחוט, אפילו כדי להשליך לכלבים, דלמא אתי למיכל, שיטעו להכשיר שחיטתן מתוך שיראו שמוסרים להן, כדפטר לקמן שחיטתן מכסוי, דלמא אתי למימר שחיטה מעלייתא היא. וניחא השתא דבאין אחרים רואין אותן עסקינן ברישא:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: Lest they spoil, etc. - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 12b) it infers from the fact that it teaches "lest they spoil" and does not teach "perhaps they spoiled," that we learn from this: one may not hand over non-sacred animals (chullin) to them ab initio (lechatchila) [to slaughter]. And Rashi explains: even if others are watching them. And this is difficult for his interpretation, for we already know this from the latter clause (seifa): "and all of them, if they slaughtered, with others watching them," etc. - which implies that it is only after the fact (bediavad) [that this is valid, not ab initio]. And one cannot say that it states "bediavad" [only] on account of [the cases of] a tamei person [slaughtering] consecrated animals, or a non-expert, while a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor (cheresh, shoteh, ve-katan) may slaughter even ab initio when others are watching them - for it is Rava who makes this inference from the fact that it does not teach "perhaps they spoiled," and according to Rava, "and all of them who slaughtered" does not refer to those [other cases] but rather to a deaf-mute, imbecile, or minor, as we say in the Gemara. And some explain that the text further on reads "Rabbah" [in place of Rava], but that Rava does not infer anything from [the distinction] between "they will spoil" and "they spoiled," just as he is not troubled by the fact that it does not teach "and if they slaughtered." And Rabbeinu Tam explains that one may not hand over chullin to them ab initio to slaughter, even in order to throw [the meat] to the dogs, lest he come to eat from it - since [others] will mistakenly come to validate their slaughter, seeing that [chullin] is handed over to them - just as, further on, their slaughter is exempted from [the requirement of] covering [the blood], lest one come to say it is a proper slaughter. And now it fits well that in the first clause (reisha) we are dealing with a case where others are not watching them.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - פירש בקונטרס דעקר ליה להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא. ולשון "כדקתני טעמא" לא משמע כפירושו. ומה שפירש נמי במסקנא גבי "דאי דיעבד תרתי דיעבד למה לי" - ואע"ג דבתמורה נמי תני והדר מפרש, התם לא תנא כי האי גוונא "הכל ממירין ותמורתן תמורה" גבי הדדי. ואי משום "לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר" משום דבעי לאסוקי "וסופג את הארבעים" לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה - אין נראה, דמשום "וסופג את הארבעים" לחודיה לא הוה ליה למיתני תרתי דיעבד, דהוה מצי למיתני "הכל ממירים והממיר סופג את הארבעים". ועוד, דבריש תמורה (דף ב.) פריך: "הכל ממירים" לכתחלה, ו"לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר" דיעבד, ומשני התם: רב יהודה הכי קתני, הכל מתפיסים בתמורה, אחד שוגג ואחד מזיד. והוה ליה לשנויי דתנא ליה משום "וסופג את הארבעים" כדפירש בקונטרס כאן. ונראה לרבינו תם, דשינויא דהכא הוי כההיא דתמורה, והכי קאמר: התם כדקתני טעמא, דלהכי תנא "הכל ממירים" דמשמע לכתחלה, לאשמעינן שאפילו המיר במזיד - דהיינו לכתחלה - מומר, דלא תימא ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר, כדאמרן בהתודה (מנחות פא.). וקשה לפירושו, דבסוף פרק קמא דתמורה (דף יג.) משמע דמן הדין ראוי להיות תמורה במזיד יותר מבשוגג, דקאמר "יהיה" לרבות שוגג כמזיד. ויש לומר, דלענין בהמה שתהא כשרה למזבח פשוט לן שוגג יותר ממזיד. אי נמי, התם איירי במזיד ולא אתרו ביה, דלא הוו ארבעים בכתפיה, וההוא מזיד פשוט לן יותר משוגג:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, as the reason is stated - Rashi explains that this comes to negate the word "all" in the first clause [of the mishnah] - that you should not say it is [permitted] ab initio (lechatchila). But the wording "as the reason is stated" does not fit his explanation. And as for what he explains also in the conclusion (maskana), regarding "if it is [valid only] after the fact (bediavad), why do I need two [statements of] bediavad" - even though in [tractate] Temurah too it teaches [the mishnah] and afterward explains it [in a similar way], there it does not teach in this manner, "all may designate temurah, and their temurah is valid," together in one clause. And if [you say the reason for repeating bediavad is] on account of [the words] "not that a person is permitted to designate temurah," because it wants to bring in "and he receives forty lashes" to teach us that one is lashed for a prohibition that involves no action - this does not seem right, for on account of "and he receives forty lashes" alone, it would not have needed to state two [instances of] bediavad, since it could have taught [simply], "all may designate temurah, and one who designates temurah receives forty lashes." And furthermore, at the beginning of [tractate] Temurah (2a) it asks: [if] "all may designate temurah" [means] ab initio, then how can [the continuation] "not that a person is permitted to designate temurah" [mean] only after the fact? And there it answers: Rav Yehuda taught it thus - "all may bring about the status of temurah," whether unwittingly or intentionally. And it should have answered [there] that it is taught this way on account of "and he receives forty lashes," as Rashi explained here. But it seems to Rabbeinu Tam that the answer here is the same as that in Temurah, and that this is what is meant: "there, as the reason is stated" - that the mishnah taught "all may designate temurah," which implies ab initio, in order to teach us that even if one designated temurah intentionally - which is equivalent to doing so ab initio - it nonetheless takes effect, lest you think that he merely receives forty lashes on his back while [the original animal] remains as it was [i.e., no temurah results], as we stated regarding the thanksgiving-offering passage (Menachot 81a). But this is difficult for his explanation, for at the end of the first chapter of Temurah (13a) it implies that, strictly speaking, a temurah made intentionally ought to be more valid than one made unwittingly, since it says that [the word] "it shall be" comes to include an unwitting [designation] just like an intentional one. And one can answer that with regard to the animal being fit for the altar, it is obvious to us [without need of a verse] that [a temurah done] unwittingly [is valid], more so than one done intentionally. Alternatively, there [in that passage] it deals with a case of intentional [designation] where the person was not forewarned, so that there are no forty lashes [administered] on his back - and that kind of intentional [designation] is more obviously [valid] to us than an unwitting one.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: וסופג את הארבעים - וא"ת: הוה ליה למימר וסופג שמונים, דהא תרי לאוי כתיב "לא יחליפנו" ו"לא ימיר". ויש לומר דחד בשלו וחד בשל חברו, כדאמר בתמורה (דף ט.), וכגון דאמר חברו "כל הרוצה להמיר בבהמתו ימיר", דבענין אחר אין ממירין בשל אחרים. והכי איתא בהדיא בתמורה פ"ק:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: And he receives the forty [lashes] - You might ask: it should have said "and he receives eighty," since two prohibitions are written: "he shall not exchange it" (lo yachalifenu) and "he shall not substitute it" (lo yamir). One may answer that one [prohibition] applies to [a case of exchanging] his own [animal], and the other to [a case of exchanging] his fellow's [animal], as stated in Temurah (9a) - namely, a case where his fellow announced, "whoever wishes to make a temurah-exchange may do so with my animal," for otherwise (i.e., without such a declaration) one cannot effect a temurah-exchange with another's animal. And this is stated explicitly in Temurah, first chapter.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: וכתיב טוב אשר לא תדור - מעיקרא מייתי מדברי תורה, והדר מייתי מדברי קבלה:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: And it is written, "It is better that you should not vow" (Ecclesiastes 5:4) - At first it brings [a proof] from the words of the Torah, and then it brings [a proof] from the words of tradition (divrei kabbalah, i.e., the Prophets and Writings).

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה שאינו נודר כל עיקר - פ"ה: דלעיל מיניה כתיב "את אשר תדור שלם", ואפילו הכי "טוב אשר לא תדור" - שמא תדור ולא תשלם. וקשה לר"ת, דלא מייתי בגמרא ההוא קרא כלל. ונראה לר"ת, דכולי מלתא דריש מהאי קרא, דהוה ליה למיכתב "טוב אשר לא תדור" משתדור, ואנא ידענא דמשתדור ולא תשלם קאמר, אלא להכי קאמר "ולא תשלם" לגלויי על "משתדור", דמשתדור כדרך הנודרין קאמר, שנודרין ומשלמין, כדאמר גבי שכיר ותושב: בא זה ולימד על זה (קדושין דף ד.):
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than both of these is one who does not vow at all - Rashi explains: the verse immediately preceding this one states, "That which you vow, pay it" (Ecclesiastes 5:3), and even so, [Scripture says] "It is better that you should not vow" - lest you vow and not pay. This is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, since the Gemara does not cite that verse [Ecclesiastes 5:3] at all. And it seems to Rabbeinu Tam that the entire matter is derived from this verse alone ["It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay"] - for it should have written "It is better that you should not vow" than "you vow" [and stopped there] - and I would understand on my own that it means "than you vow and do not pay." Rather, it says "and do not pay" specifically in order to reveal something about [the word] "than you vow": that "than you vow" is speaking of the ordinary manner of vowers - that they vow and then pay. [The two phrases mutually clarify one another,] as is said regarding [the terms] "a hired worker" and "a resident": "this one comes and teaches about that one" (Kiddushin 4a).
